name: Isis
label: Hydra Head
lede: Two roommates in Boston, a label run out of a bedroom, and a decade of records that gave post-metal its map.

eras.title: Roommates with a stack of amps
eras.text: Aaron Turner and Jeff Caxide started Isis in Boston as roommates and spent two years churning through members before the five-piece that would make every album settled. The first records came out on small labels, one of them Turner's own Hydra Head.

years.src: Wikipedia: Isis (band) · Riot Fest: Autodiscography · Wikipedia: Aaron Turner
years.h: Isis starts in Boston with Turner, Caxide, Harris and Mereschuk
years.p: [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] and [[Jeff Caxide|bf6fad81-e874-43af-a617-cdfe080ec108]] form the band with drummer [[Aaron Harris|eaa40a05-ea31-49a4-9007-4908334c89d3]] and Chris Mereschuk on electronics and vocals.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band's formation to autumn 1997. Turner has said Caxide was his roommate at the start, and that he did not want to sing but got the job because nobody else would take it.

Turner was already running Hydra Head Records, the label he started in 1993 as a mail-order business while still in high school in New Mexico. Isis would spend years as one of its best-known acts.

years.h: First show: Montreal, a city the band would circle back to
years.p: Isis plays its first show in Montreal in spring 1998. Twelve years later it would close its career in the same city.
years.xp:
Wikipedia places the debut in Montreal in spring 1998 and notes the band chose the same city for its final show on June 23, 2010.

Turner has described the first tour that followed as one that nearly broke the band up, before he and Caxide decided to carry on.

years.h: Guitarist Randy Larsen of Cable joins the East Coast tour, Mereschuk leaves
years.p: After a summer 1998 East Coast run with Randy Larsen from Cable on guitar, Chris Mereschuk leaves the band.

years.h: Mosquito Control EP arrives on Escape Artist
years.p: The first Isis release is a short EP that plants the mosquito, an image that keeps returning in the band's artwork and themes.

years.h: Michael Gallagher and Jay Randall join for The Red Sea
years.p: [[Michael Gallagher|d491377d-0300-4a36-b519-535ac1b4c631]], from Cast Iron Hike, and Jay Randall, later of Agoraphobic Nosebleed, join and record The Red Sea.

years.h: The Red Sea EP, on Second Nature
years.p: The EP is the first record with Gallagher, and it is the last Isis release with Jay Randall.

years.h: Sawblade: a first release on Turner's own Hydra Head
years.p: The Sawblade EP appears in 1999 on Hydra Head Records, the label Turner ran alongside the band.

years.h: Bryant Clifford Meyer replaces Randall, and the line-up locks
years.p: [[Bryant Clifford Meyer|22c39a7c-d513-4091-8065-122bc8ebe68e]], previously of The Gersch, joins on guitar and keyboards. The five of them then make every Isis album.
years.xp: Turner has said it took until 1999 to settle the line-up because of transient members and personality clashes. Turner, Caxide, Harris, Gallagher and Meyer stayed together until the end in 2010.

eras.title: A slow, heavy first album
eras.text: Celestial put the band's long-form, tidal approach on record for the first time, and a side project with a hero from the Neurosis camp made the Isis sound larger.

years.h: Celestial is the debut album, on Escape Artist and Hydra Head
years.p: Recorded in January and February 2000 at The Outpost in Stoughton, Massachusetts, with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] engineering and mixing.

years.h: Isis and Pig Destroyer split on Relapse
years.p: A split release with Pig Destroyer arrives in July 2000 on Relapse.

years.src: Wikipedia: Celestial (Isis album) · Riot Fest: Autodiscography
years.h: SGNL›05 EP on Neurot, with a Justin Broadrick remix
years.p: Neurot Recordings, the label tied to [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]], puts out an EP from the Celestial sessions. Godflesh's Justin Broadrick remixes the title track.
years.xp: Turner has called the EP part of the same whole as Celestial. Neurosis was one of the bands he names as a founding influence, along with Earth and Buzzoven.

eras.title: Oceanic, then the panopticon
eras.text: Two records in two years turned Isis from a heavy band into the reference point for post-metal. Oceanic reached for water and ambient space. Panopticon took on surveillance and got a guest from Tool.

years.h: Oceanic: the record fans still name first
years.p: Recorded April and May 2002 at Fort Apache in Cambridge and New Alliance in Boston, with Matt Bayles producing. Maria Christopher of 27 sings on three songs.
years.xp:
Oceanic is a concept album. Turner described in radio interviews and in the booklet a story of a man who drowns himself after finding out about his partner's relationship with her brother. Wikipedia notes Terrorizer ranked it the top album of 2002, and Rolling Stone placed it 72nd on its 2017 list of the 100 greatest metal albums.

Turner has called it the band's quintessential album. The song Weight was later heard in the TV series Friday Night Lights.

years.h: The band moves to Los Angeles
years.p: Isis relocates to Los Angeles after several years in Boston.

years.h: Panopticon: a record about being watched
years.p: Recorded at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles in June and July 2004. Justin Chancellor of [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]] plays on the instrumental Altered Course.
years.xp:
The title comes from Jeremy Bentham's prison design and Michel Foucault's writing on surveillance. The liner notes bring in the technology writer Howard Rheingold and the futurist Alex Steffen. The cover is an aerial photograph of South San Bruno and South San Francisco, and Turner said the link to the themes was intentional but meant to be subtle.

Wikipedia reports it reached number 47 on Billboard's Top Independent Albums.

years.h: A free show at the Los Angeles Museum of Contemporary Art
years.p: Isis plays at the museum in support of an exhibition of 1950s and 60s minimalist art.

years.h: Revolver ranks Isis twelfth-heaviest band ever
years.p: Revolver puts the band at number twelve on its list of the heaviest bands, in December 2004.

eras.title: Sharing stages with Tool
eras.text: Isis played its biggest rooms, put out its most melodic album, and had mixed feelings about the attention. Turner has said he preferred smaller venues.

years.cap: Isis opening for Tool Bakersfield, CA September, 2006 · Wikimedia
years.h: Isis plays all of Oceanic at KOKO in London
years.p: The band performs the album front to back for All Tomorrow's Parties' Don't Look Back series. The recording is released as Live V.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the show as July 23, 2006 at KOKO. The recording came out in 2009 as Live V.

years.h: Isis opens for Tool across North America
years.p: The band supports Tool's tour for 10,000 Days and plays to far bigger crowds than usual.
years.xp: Turner has said the Tool audiences were positive, with only minimal heckling across the whole tour. He also said he preferred smaller rooms, where he felt a better connection between player, music and listener.

years.src: Wikipedia: In the Absence of Truth
years.h: In the Absence of Truth: the melodic turn
years.p: Recorded in June and July 2006 and produced by the band and Matt Bayles, with more clean singing than before.
years.xp: It runs nearly 65 minutes, the band's longest record. No lyrics were printed, but Turner confirmed a concept drawn from Hassan-i-Sabbah, Don Quixote, House of Leaves and Labyrinths. Wikipedia lists the peak as number 6 on Billboard's Top Heatseekers and 20 on Top Independent Albums.
play: Not in Rivers, but in Drops

eras.title: Said everything they wanted to say
eras.text: Wavering Radiant was the band's chart peak, made with a new producer, and then the five of them announced it was over and went home to Montreal.

years.h: Wavering Radiant and a new producer
years.p: Joe Barresi replaces Matt Bayles, whose work the band felt had become routine. Tool's Adam Jones plays on two songs.
years.xp: Vinyl came out April 21, with the CD on May 5. Sessions ran November 2008 to January 2009, largely at Sound City in Van Nuys, and the album drew on Carl Jung's Memories, Dreams, Reflections. Turner kept a dream journal and stopped smoking marijuana in 2008 to remember his dreams. It debuted at number 98 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Golden Gods: best underground metal act
years.p: Revolver's Golden Gods awards name Isis best underground metal act in April 2009.

years.big: Done, and on their own terms
q: We've done everything we wanted to do, said everything we wanted to say.
years.h: The band calls it
years.p: Isis announces it is ending, with the same five members who made every album.
years.xp: The final tours took in Bonnaroo and Australia's Soundwave, with bands including Baroness, Big Business, Cave In and Melvins. Turner has said the band taking up so much of his time was frustrating and kept him from other projects.

years.cap: Bryant Clifford Meyer, guitarist and keyboardist of Californian post-metal ba... · Wikimedia
years.h: Last show: Montreal, where it started
years.p: Isis plays its final show in the city of its first one.

years.h: Melvins / Isis split lands on Hydra Head
years.p: Isis contributes Way Through Woven Branches and The Pliable Foe, both from the Wavering Radiant sessions. The Melvins supported Isis on farewell dates.

eras.title: After the tide
eras.text: The five went in different directions, with Turner into Mamiffer, Sumac and more Old Man Gloom and the rest into Palms, until one benefit night in 2018.

years.h: Caxide, Harris and Meyer start Palms with Deftones' Chino Moreno
years.p: [[Palms|9c651ba1-59d3-4772-9fed-cd233af44465]] forms in 2011 with [[Chino Moreno|e61400d1-9434-4abc-ac7a-4f1dad60cfc7]] on vocals and guitar. Caxide joins in April 2012 by Wikipedia's account, and the self-titled debut arrives on June 25, 2013.

years.h: Temporal gathers demos and unreleased material
years.p: A double album of demos, unreleased tracks and remixes on Ipecac.

years.h: Turner announces the wind-down of Hydra Head
years.p: Turner announces the imminent demise of Hydra Head Records. The label folded in 2020 by Wikipedia's account.

years.h: Celestial, Panopticon and Oceanic come back remastered
years.p: Ipecac reissues them with new artwork by Turner: Celestial (2013), Panopticon (April 29, 2014) and Oceanic (November 4, 2014).

years.h: The band changes its social media name
years.p: With the rise of the Islamic State, the band changes its online name to Isis the Band.
years.xp: Turner has said the confusion made things hard. He says he appreciates fans who still wear Isis gear, and calls it an act of courage.

years.h: Turner forms Sumac
years.p: After [[Mamiffer|e26aea76-9a1e-4bfa-ac61-26f723abde6e]] and [[Old Man Gloom|75a97901-0051-4b67-a79b-9ebf2400d1d9]], [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] starts [[Sumac|9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f]] in 2014.

years.src: Treble · Wikipedia: Old Man Gloom · Wikipedia: Isis (band)
years.h: Isis returns for one night, billed as Celestial
years.p: All five play the Wiltern in Los Angeles as Celestial, a benefit for Cave In's late Caleb Scofield, with Cave In, Pelican, Old Man Gloom and 27 on the bill.
years.xp: Scofield, of Cave In and Old Man Gloom, died March 28, 2018 at age 39 in a car accident in New Hampshire, according to Wikipedia. Treble reported that proceeds went to his family. The five members performed under the name Celestial rather than Isis.
